prompts.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve.
Create a professional 2D hand-drawn fighting game SPRITE ANIMATION ATLAS of the EXACT female swordswoman Tsukiyo from the reference image. Reference role: authoritative character design and ink rendering. Preserve her narrow adult face, high very long ponytail tied with light ribbon, light draping kimono sleeves, dark pleated hakama, wrapped forearms, sandals, and exactly one long curved tachi held with two hands. White and gray expressive Japanese ink strokes with opaque black inside the clothing, genuinely TRANSPARENT outside silhouettes. No colored pixels, no shadow plane, no background, no text, no labels, no borders or grid lines.
Layout is CRITICAL: landscape 2048x1024 canvas, EXACTLY FOUR equal columns and TWO equal rows, eight 512x512 rectangular animation cells. ONE complete, separate full-body character per cell. All face RIGHT in the same slight three-quarter side view. Fixed orthographic camera. In EACH cell the pelvis horizontal center is x=200 relative to cell left, feet baseline y=460, top of ponytail roughly y=65, adult body from head to feet height ~340. Character and entire sword must remain within cell with 20px empty margin. Sword can reach x=490 but never cross a cell boundary. Keep exactly the same character size and face in all cells.
Frame order left-to-right then top-to-bottom:
1: original calm lunar guard, both hands near waist, sword diagonally up-right, feet spread but narrow enough for a fighting stance.
2: same guard, slight natural breath in shoulders, sleeve and ponytail settle; feet EXACTLY same place as frame1; do not scale whole figure.
3: walking cycle A: front right foot forward touching ground, back heel raised, hands and blade steady in guard.
4: walking cycle B: body transferring weight, back foot lifts, bending knee visible under hakama.
5: walking cycle C: passing stance feet close, lifting foot passes.
6: walking cycle D: other leg extends forward and lands, sleeves lag gently.
7: walking cycle E: opposite weight transfer, back heel lifts.
8: walking cycle F: opposite passing stance, returning smoothly into frame3.
Motion must be actual anatomical changes to limbs, folds and hair, not translated or rotated copies of the same illustration. No extra weapons, duplicate limbs, slash trails, ornamental scenery or changes of costume. This is a usable registration-consistent sprite atlas, not a character concept sheet.

Use case: identity-preserve. Produce a transparent 2D fighting-game sprite atlas of Tsukiyo, EXACTLY the woman in the reference (authoritative character design): narrow adult face, very long high ponytail with ribbon, light flowing kimono sleeves, black pleated hakama, wrapped forearms, sandals, one long tachi in BOTH hands. Detailed white/gray Japanese ink with opaque black garment interiors; true transparency outside silhouettes. No text, lines, backgrounds, shadows, red pixels or decorative effects.
Layout: EXACTLY 4 columns by 2 rows, eight equal square cells, 2048x1024 landscape canvas. Every character faces RIGHT, same orthographic 3/4 side camera and consistent proportions. Each cell contains ONE full body and the entire sword. IMPORTANT leave large empty margins: body upright height about 300px within the 512px cell; feet at y=460; head around y=150; pelvis near x=170. Both feet registered at x=120 and x=235, baseline460 in ALL EIGHT FRAMES. Never move feet, scale the person, crop a ponytail or sword, or cross cell boundaries. At maximum thrust the blade tip stays left of x=495. Consistent sword length across all frames.
Eight successive frames of ONE controlled TWO-HANDED HORIZONTAL THRUST at the opponent's chest. Read left-to-right, top row then bottom:
1 guarded pose, both hands near abdomen and blade diagonal upward right.
2 anticipation: elbows fold, hands pull toward the left hip, blade rotates toward horizontal.
3 fully chambered: hilt near left lower ribs, blade exactly horizontal pointing right, weight on back leg.
4 forward extension: elbows halfway straightening, both hands push right, torso turns and inclines slightly right.
5 decisive contact: both arms extended right from chest, ONE rigid near-horizontal blade points right, front knee bends, back leg grounded. NO duplicate blade, no motion trails.
6 follow-through: extension held, sleeves and ponytail catch up, blade still horizontal.
7 withdrawal: elbows bend, both hands recover toward abdomen, tip rises slightly.
8 recovered original lunar guard matching frame1, fabric settles.
Draw genuine anatomical changes, elbow articulation, wrist alignment, turning torso, cloth drag, stable face. Preserve the original character's beautiful detailed ink rendering. These are eight discrete registered full-body animation cels, not eight character redesigns.

Use case: precise-object-edit. EDIT TARGET: Image 2 is an eight-frame Tsukiyo thrust animation sheet. Image 1 is authoritative character design. Correct ONLY the sheet layout and weapon clipping; preserve all eight body poses and rendering from Image2.
The current sheet clips the sword in extended thrust frames. Re-layout these same EIGHT poses into EXACTLY TWO COLUMNS and FOUR ROWS on a SQUARE 2048x2048 transparent canvas. Each of the eight cells must be a WIDE rectangle 1024x512. This is vital: TWO characters across, FOUR characters down, NOT four across. Within each cell put the character's pelvis at x=350, feet baseline y=465 and top of ponytail y=50. Leave broad transparent space to the RIGHT for the whole sword. All body sizes identical. Each cell contains one entire character, both feet, all hair, both hands, a single hilt, and the COMPLETE long gently curved tachi blade with its pointed tip. At full extension blade ends at x=900, leaving at least 100px clear space to the right cell boundary. Reconstruct the missing distal blade and tip in poses4,5,6. SAME physical sword length in every cell, as the guard sword in image1; one sharp blade, no doubled outlines, no trails. Both hands on one hilt. Feet stay registered, identical standing leg length across frames, no zoom.
Pose order row-major: 1 guard; 2 chambering low; 3 chambered horizontal; 4 beginning extension; 5 full chest-height horizontal thrust; 6 same full extension with sleeve follow-through; 7 withdrawing; 8 recovered guard.
Keep face, kimono folds, hakama, hair and white-gray ink rendering intact. Black inside clothing remains opaque, outside silhouettes genuinely transparent. NO grid lines, NO text, NO scenery, NO cropping. Priority: fully visible constant-length sword and full-body registration.

Use case: identity-preserve. Create a production sprite atlas of the EXACT Tsukiyo from the reference, drawn in the SAME detailed monochrome Japanese ink, same adult face, high long ponytail, white draped kimono, black pleated hakama, wrapped forearms, sandals and ONE tachi held in both hands. TRUE transparent background outside each figure, opaque black within clothing.
MANDATORY LAYOUT: square canvas, a visible thin light gray rectilinear grid divides it into EXACTLY 2 equal columns and 4 equal rows, EIGHT equal wide rectangular panels. Draw straight thin grid boundaries so cells are unambiguous; NO text or numbers. Keep each entire figure and entire sword INSIDE its own panel with generous clear margins on ALL FOUR SIDES. No body part touches a grid line. Subject height no more than 65% of cell height, even smaller if needed to fit raised sword. Do not fill the cells edge-to-edge. Identical scale/proportions across all eight figures. Every figure faces RIGHT, fixed 3/4 side camera, full body. The feet baseline at 85% of each cell's height. Pelvis x=36% of cell width. One sharp constant-length sword; no motion trails or extra weapons.
Read panels left-to-right, top-to-bottom:
1 (row1 left) anticipation of rising slash: knees bend, two hands near right knee, sword low diagonal down-right.
2 (row1 right) rising cut halfway: legs extend, hands move upward, sword diagonal right at waist height.
3 (row2 left) rising cut finish: torso tall, both hands near face, sword rises diagonally high-right, entire sword including point fits fully INSIDE this panel.
4 (row2 right) recovery: arms lower from high guard toward abdomen, blade diagonal up-right.
5 (row3 left) anticipation low cut: feet wide, knees lower, hilt near left hip, blade points horizontally right at waist height.
6 (row3 right) active low slash: deep knee bend, hands extend right, sword horizontal right at opponent's knee height, no floor contact.
7 (row4 left) low cut follow-through: hips turned, arms extended low, long sleeve swings after hands, grounded both feet.
8 (row4 right) recover upright lunar guard, sword diagonal up-right, sleeves settle.
Animate limbs and body honestly, maintain Tsukiyo's identity, clean contour and detailed fabric. GRID MUST STAY EMPTY AROUND ALL CHARACTERS; allow extra empty space rather than clipping or drawing across neighboring panels.

Use case: background-extraction. Edit this atlas by REMOVING ONLY THE PANEL BORDERS and all extraneous background debris, gray rectangles, white framing paint, detached marks around the edges and white blobs outside the eight character silhouettes. Return a genuinely transparent-background atlas. Do NOT redraw, resize, reposition, crop, rotate or rearrange the eight women or their swords. Preserve exact canvas size and each woman's exact coordinates and pose. Preserve opaque black garment interiors. Preserve all fine hair and fabric details attached to each character. Keep the feet and sword tips complete. The entire surrounding area, including what used to be the cell borders, must be empty transparent alpha with no marks whatsoever. Eight clean cutout sprites in the same two-column four-row arrangement, no grid and no text.

Use case: identity-preserve. Image1 is Tsukiyo's authoritative design. Image2 shows the required clean sprite-atlas layout and rendering. Create a NEW eight-frame atlas of her AIRBORNE poses in precisely that TWO COLUMNS / FOUR ROWS arrangement on a square transparent canvas. Same detailed white-gray Japanese ink, adult face, high long ponytail, kimono, black pleated hakama, forearm wraps, sandals, one constant-length tachi in both hands. No scenery, no grid lines, no words, no colored pixels, no shadows or detached marks.
Every wide rectangular cell must have at least 20px clear transparent margin on all sides. Each full body AND entire sword fits inside its cell. Relative to a 627x313 cell: pelvis at x=300, virtual floor y=290; upright equivalent body height250. Keep that scale even when knees fold. All face RIGHT in a consistent side three-quarter view. Do not fill every cell with the silhouette; keep the figure small enough for the entire blade. Large empty space to the right of the body for attacks. No clipping!
ROW1: left = jump ascent, both knees softly bent, feet tucked a little, sword in lunar guard, kimono and ponytail trail downward; right = descending from jump, legs reach toward landing, sleeves and ponytail float upward.
ROW2: left = airborne thrust preparation, knees bent and both hands chamber near abdomen with sword pointing horizontally right; right = airborne thrust contact, both arms extend and a single sword points horizontal-right at opponent's torso, legs still bent.
ROW3: left = airborne slash preparation, both hands above right shoulder, blade high diagonally right, whole tip visible; right = airborne slash contact, sword angled down-right in front of torso, kimono follows rotating shoulders.
ROW4: left = overhead descending cut preparation, both hands high, knees folded, whole blade up-right within cell; right = descending cut contact, torso inclined forward, both hands press downward, sword steep diagonal down-right toward opponent below, legs tucked back. Entire tip must remain above the bottom of the cell. Make real limb/body changes and retain identical facial identity.
Keep the careful clean transparent spacing of Image2, not a poster.

Use case: identity-preserve. Make an eight-pose transparent sprite atlas of Tsukiyo, exact adult character from reference1, same white/gray Japanese ink linework, long high ponytail tied with ribbon, light kimono sleeves, dark hakama, forearm wraps, sandals, ONE tachi. Reference2 is rendering and clean two-column/four-row layout. Match it. Square canvas with EXACTLY 2 columns and 4 rows of WIDE rectangular cells, no visible grid. Genuinely transparent around silhouettes, opaque blacks inside clothing. NO text, background marks, panels, shadows or blood.
Each pose is a complete full body in fixed side-three-quarter camera, facing RIGHT, full sword visible. Keep original body proportions and consistent anatomical size, do NOT enlarge crouching or fallen figures to fill their cell. Leave a generous empty transparent horizontal band between every row. Standing-equivalent height is 65% of cell height. Floor at 85% of each cell height. Pelvis near 40% of cell width for standing poses.
Row1 left: sprint contact pose, torso leaning forward, front foot planted far ahead, back leg extending, sword held near hip pointing diagonal forward, ponytail and sleeves stream behind.
Row1 right: sprint passing pose, opposite knee driving forward, other foot pushes off, same torso inclination, hands and sword stable, fabric follows.
Row2 left: dodge anticipation, knees start folding, hips sink, sword held diagonal forward protectively.
Row2 right: deep grounded evasive crouch, torso lowered to waist height, front knee bent, rear leg bracing, head tucked, blade held horizontal toward right, ponytail follows low.
Row3 left: recovery from crouch, rising through bent knees, arms draw sword into lunar guard.
Row3 right: defeat beginning, knees buckle, torso curls forward, head lowers, still holding sword, no gore.
Row4 left: falling sideways toward the RIGHT, one knee and one hand touch floor, torso at 45 degrees, blade lowered safely away from torso, hair falls forward.
Row4 right: final defeated pose lying naturally on the ground on her side, legs bent, long ponytail spread left, the ONE sword lies along the ground to the right near her hand. Not kneeling, not standing. Keep SAME character scale as above so the horizontal figure is wider but shorter.
No rigid rotations of a standing illustration: anatomically redraw knees, spine, elbows, hair and fabric for every pose. Every entire body and weapon must fit its own cell without touching neighboring sprites.
